# upscale_review

**In one sentence:** The Upscale Review modal, where you choose per image (or per size tier) whether it is upscaled, cleaned up from JPEG to PNG at the same size, or left alone.

## Why it exists
The upscale pipeline step (`prepare_lora_kit/steps/upscale/`) finds images that are too small, or JPEGs that could be cleaned. Before it spends GPU time, it pauses and asks the user. This folder is that question in the desktop UI.

## What's inside
| File / folder | What it does |
|---|---|
| `upscale_review.js` | `showUpscaleReview(pending, { onSubmitted })` sets the starting decisions, groups items into tiers, builds the cards and tier sections, handles selection and the per-tier presets, and submits. |
| `upscale_review.css` | Styles for the workspace, tier sections, cards, detail panel, decision pill and metrics (`.upscale-*`). |
| `components/` | Modal frame, tier section, image card and detail panel. |
| `utils/` | Decision rules, tier grouping and display formatting. |

## How it works
- The job controller calls this for a pending interaction of kind `upscale_review`. The payload `items` include `path`, `uri`/`thumb_uri`/`view_uri`, `width`/`height`, `min_side`, `target`, `threshold`, `is_jpeg`, `tier_lo`/`tier_hi` and `initial_decision`.
- Each image starts on its normalized `initial_decision`. The first image of the smallest tier is selected.
- The "Upscale all" and "Keep size" buttons apply a preset to every image in that tier, then redraw.
- "Continue" sends `{ decisions: { path: "upscale" | "cleanup" | "skip" } }` through `api().submit_interaction`. Cancel closes the modal without an answer.

## Who uses it
- `static/job/controller.js`: calls it for `pending.kind === "upscale_review"`.
- `static/styles.css`: `@import`s `upscale_review.css`.
- Python side: `prepare_lora_kit_ui/runner/interactions.py` (`UiInteractionProvider.upscale_review`).
- Tests: `tests/ui/static/upscale_review.test.js`. The Python tier logic is tested in `tests/steps/upscale/test_review.py`.

## Good to know
- `upscale_review.css` defines `.upscale-detail-actions` and `.upscale-detail-actions button` twice (around lines 143 and 270). The later block overrides the grid columns of the earlier one.
